Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2), a redesigned customer dashboard with a light/dark theme system (`html[data-theme="light"]`, toggled via components/nx/ThemeToggle.tsx, tokens in app/globals.css). This is a READ-ONLY visual-consistency AUDIT before production promotion — absolutely do NOT edit or fix anything, just report findings with file:line evidence. This is important: just report, do not touch code.

CRITICAL, non-negotiable constraint: components/nx/RackHero.tsx and components/nx/Ribbons.tsx (the dashboard's aurora ribbon-stream background) were explicitly reverted to their original pre-session state per a direct, emphatic owner instruction after repeated automated "fixes" made them worse. DO NOT suggest changes to these two files, DO NOT flag their current light-mode appearance as a "bug" even if it looks visually different from other light-mode surfaces — they are intentionally frozen. If you notice anything about them, do not mention it at all in your report.

Your job: spot-check for LEFTOVER light/dark theme bugs across the dashboard that may have been missed in the many rounds of fixes already done this session. Specifically:

1. Search app/globals.css and components/nx/*, components/customer/* for any use of bare `bg-white`/`text-white`/`border-white` (NOT `bg-white/NN` with an opacity suffix) OUTSIDE of `.nx-dark-island` scopes — these are suspicious because `--color-white` is deliberately flipped to mean "ink" in light mode, so a bare `bg-white` outside a dark-locked island will invert unexpectedly. List any you find with file:line, and say whether it looks intentional (a toggle knob, a checkmark badge meant to stay literally white) or looks like a missed case.

2. Search for any component using inline hardcoded hex/rgb colors (e.g. `style={{ color: '#...' }}` or `className="text-[#...]"`) that do NOT have a corresponding light-mode override nearby or an obvious reason to be theme-invariant — these are exactly the kind of thing that silently breaks in one theme.

3. Check components/nx/Shell.tsx and components/nx/Banners.tsx (VerifyEmailBanner, ImpersonationBanner) for light-mode readability — these render on EVERY dashboard page so a bug here is maximally visible.

4. Grep for any remaining TODO/FIXME comments related to "light mode", "dark mode", or "theme" anywhere under components/nx, components/customer, app/dashboard, app/globals.css — list them verbatim with file:line, these are self-admitted gaps.

5. Separately (not theme-related): check app/admin and app/staff pages/components briefly — these are supposed to have been explicitly kept on "the original design, whatever the theme" (per a git commit titled "Keep /admin and /staff on the original design, whatever the theme" — commit 26c941b). Confirm this is still true: do admin/staff pages import any components/nx/* styling, or are they still fully isolated from the Nexion theme system? A leak here would mean the admin panel accidentally inherited light/dark theming it wasn't supposed to.

Report as a short list of concrete findings grouped by category above, each with file:line and a one-sentence description. If a category has nothing, say "clean." Keep total report under 600 words. Absolutely no edits.

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - **Do not** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - **Do not** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

## Visual-Consistency Audit — Findings

**1. Bare `bg-white`/`text-white`/`border-white` outside `.nx-dark-island`**

Confirmed via `app/globals.css:298` that bare `text-white`/`bg-white` (no opacity suffix) is an *intentional* mechanism — `--color-white` flips to ink in light mode by design, and `--color-navy-950` flips to paper (`app/globals.css:305`) as its paired counterpart. `border-white` (bare) does not occur anywhere in `components/nx`/`components/customer`. Spot-checked ~650 bare `text-white` hits — all sampled read as plain heading/label ink, consistent with the documented intent. Two things worth a manual eyeball, not clear bugs:
- `components/nx/SettingsView.tsx:120` — toggle-knob `bg-white` (no opacity suffix). Flips to ink in light mode instead of staying a literal white knob; still has contrast against its track, but is the "toggle knob" pattern flagged as worth checking. Same pattern repeats at `components/customer/DomainControls.tsx:52`, `DomainRedirects.tsx:207`, `DomainAdvanced.tsx:189`, `SslManager.tsx:136`, `GameDeployWizard.tsx:1686`, `components/nx/DeployView.tsx:843`.
- `components/customer/AddStorage.tsx:143` and `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:1336` — `"bg-white text-navy-950"` selected-pill state. Because both tokens flip together (white→ink, navy-950→paper), light mode renders an ink pill with white text — inverted from dark mode's white-pill/navy-text but still high-contrast. Likely fine, not a bug.

**2. Hardcoded hex/rgb without light-mode counterpart**

- `components/customer/StripeCheckoutModal.tsx:65` — `<div className="rounded-xl bg-white p-1">` wraps the embedded Stripe checkout iframe. `bg-white` here uses the token (flips to ink `#0a1829` in light mode), while the outer dialog (`bg-navy-950`, line 52) flips to paper/white. Result: a dark box framing Stripe's own white checkout UI inside an otherwise white modal — looks like a missed case; this one wants a literal white background, not the token.
- `components/nx/WhatsNewView.tsx:236`, `RewardsView.tsx:207/235/245`, `Banners.tsx` accent rules, `BillingView.tsx:525-526`, `PaymentTrustBar.tsx:37-66`, `ItemIcon.tsx:389/397` — all hardcoded hex, but these are decorative glows or fixed brand marks (Visa/Mastercard/Google logos, badge accents) explicitly documented or clearly theme-invariant by nature. Clean.
- `components/nx/Banners.tsx:141` (`background`/`color` both `#d623e1` on the impersonation "live dot") is correct, not a bug — `.dot-live::after` (`app/globals.css:2102-2106`) consumes `currentColor`, so setting both properties to the same value is the intended technique.

**3. Shell.tsx / Banners.tsx readability**

Real bug: `VerifyEmailBanner` and `ImpersonationBanner` (`components/nx/Banners.tsx:84-160`, via the shared `Banner` wrapper at lines 32-78) paint a **hardcoded** dark-navy background (`rgba(1,15,34,0.86)` line 48, `rgba(1,15,34,0.88)` line 134) that does not move with theme. They're rendered from `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:204,213` as children inside `<Shell>`'s plain `<main>` (`components/nx/Shell.tsx:322-333`), which is **not** `.nx-dark-island`-scoped (only the rail/header are, `Shell.tsx:212,227,242`). Their headline text uses `text-white`/`text-tx-body`, which flip to near-black ink in light mode — producing near-invisible dark-on-dark text ("Confirm your email address", the impersonation target email) in light mode. `NotificationsPanel` (also in Banners.tsx) is unaffected since it's rendered inside the `.nx-dark-island` header (`Shell.tsx:242,274`).

Aside: `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:186-188` has a stale comment claiming the impersonation banner is "not drawn here," directly contradicted by line 204 rendering it — not theme-related but worth a cleanup note.

**4. TODO/FIXME for light/dark/theme**

Clean — no matches under `components/nx`, `components/customer`, `app/dashboard`, or `app/globals.css`.

**5. Admin/staff isolation**

Confirmed intact. `app/admin/layout.tsx:21` and `app/staff/layout.tsx:8` import `components/portal/Shell`, not `components/nx/*`; no file under `app/admin` or `app/staff` imports anything from `components/nx`. The CSS mechanism at `app/globals.css:540-546` (`html[data-theme="light"]:has(.nx-dark-island.min-h-screen) body`) exists specifically to keep that shell's body dark regardless of `data-theme`, matching commit 26c941b's intent. No leak found.
